question: A 640 metre long train travelling at 80 km/h overtook a 540 metre long train travelling at 72 km/h in the same direction. How long did it take the faster train to cross the other train completely?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 80 − 72 = 8 km/h

Relative speed in m/s = 8 × 5/18 = 20/9 m/s

Total distance to cover = 640 + 540 = 1180 m

Time = 1180 ÷ (20/9) = 59 × 9 = 531 seconds

531 seconds = 8 minutes 51 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 8 minutes 51 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of faster train (L₁) = 640 m

Length of slower train (L₂) = 540 m

Speed of faster train (S₁) = 80 km/h

Speed of slower train (S₂) = 72 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 
• 
 
 Train 1: 640m
 
 Train 2: 540m
 

 S1 = 80 km/h
 

 S2 = 72 km/h
 Relative Speed = S1 − S2 (Same Direction)
 Total Distance = 640 + 540 = 1180 m

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance to be covered = L₁ + L₂ = 640 + 540 = 1180 m

⇒ Relative speed = 80 − 72 = 8 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 8 × (5/18) = 40/18 = 20/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken = 1180 ÷ (20/9)

⇒ Time taken = 1180 × 9/20

⇒ Time taken = 59 × 9 = 531 seconds

⇒ Time in minutes = 531 ÷ 60 = 8 minutes and 51 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 8 minutes 51 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their speeds. When they move in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Distance

When a train crosses another train, a bridge, or a platform, the total distance covered is the sum of the lengths of the two objects.</p
